turei-zahav.1#א: One may not rely on him. Explanation: to buy from him.
turei-zahav.1#ב: And some say even from one who is not suspected, etc. Darkei Moshe wrote: however the custom is not so, but we presume every person in a presumption of kosher status; and since the Rav did not write here it appears we should not practice so; and it is correct, especially as we see corruption of generations and I do not presume the generation kosher.
turei-zahav.2#א: One dines with him. For even though he is suspected — "before the blind do not place a stumbling block" — nevertheless he himself is not suspected to eat it.
turei-zahav.2#ב: Transgressing a sin for appetite. The honor of the Rav is in its place and his words are astounding in this gloss, for in Rashba that Beit Yosef brought it is written that one who transgresses one of the transgressions is believed in other prohibitions, and all the more if he does so for appetite, etc.; if so why did the Rav write this gloss — if he is presumed to transgress other prohibitions, even not for appetite he is believed for this prohibition; and if presumed regarding this prohibition, even for appetite certainly he is not believed. What Beit Yosef wrote below in this siman in the name of Rashba that a habitual sinner for appetite is believed even for that matter, like Rava in the first chapter of Chullin, end of his words — meaning there is leniency when permitted and forbidden are before him he does not abandon the permitted and eat forbidden; but otherwise forbidden, as Tur siman 2 wrote that without knife checking forbidden to eat from his slaughter; here too how may they eat with him lest there was no permitted before him and he ate forbidden — how may others eat with him; if so this is not called suspected as the Rav said, and certainly this gloss has no explanation. What is harder: we never find that suspected is worse than transgressing for appetite — if you say there he is suspected meaning he instructs so intentionally even when permitted is before him he abandons it and eats forbidden, then he is like a full gentile, as Rama wrote in siman 2 regarding one who eats nevelah not for appetite; how can Rashbag in chapter Ad Kamah rule that one suspected regarding something may judge and testify. Also proof from what Terumat HaDeshen wrote: if you suspect him for this you suspect him as a full gentile intending to mislead, end of his words; and if you say suspected means he is not concerned for prohibition at all, in truth he is like a full gentile as we said; plainly he is not worse than transgressing for appetite — if so what does it mean he is not called suspected. Darkei Moshe in Hagahot Asheri: one suspected of a prohibition forbidden to eat with him — even permitted things, lest he feed forbidden too, end of his words.
turei-zahav.3#_: Behold he gave to his mother-in-law suspected regarding the prohibition — forbidden, for she is ashamed before her son-in-law, etc.; so it must be.
turei-zahav.4#א: Suspected also regarding it. Explanation: penalty — suspected that he will not sell at all even if he did not want to sell only for himself.
turei-zahav.4#ב: To come buy, etc. In chapter Ad Kamah (Bechorot 30) the Gemara: that butcher was suspected to sell fat, etc.; Rava penalized him even regarding nuts, etc.; difficult for Tur why he wrote the prohibition was with nuts that enticed youths — the Gemara's style differs; we need two elements: sale done through sin, and penalty for future suspicion; Tur notes what was needed for sinful sale; Gemara notes what connects to later suspicion via nuts; we penalize for teaching theft perhaps; Tur did not need to say he enticed youths — proved from "children run after nuts"; end of my explanation reconciling Tur and Gemara. Difficulty on Beit Yosef who wrote halachah is like R' Shimon — in Eruvin we conclude like R' Yehudah against R' Shimon as Rosh wrote; nevertheless here Beit Yosef well aimed halachah like R' Shimon for another reason since Rava holds like him as I said.
turei-zahav.5#_: Suspected regarding the light. Explanation: when he has benefit from it he is not believed to buy from him; but without his benefit we say a habitual sinner for one matter is not a habitual sinner for other transgressions except Shabbat and idolatry as seif 12; likewise Perishah; and Beit Yosef end of this siman distinguishes one food type vs two types.
turei-zahav.7#_: One who is suspected regarding a matter, etc. Also wondrous is Rama's view to me — Rashba in responsum Beit Yosef brought only for testimony disqualification, as he brings later for cemetery on eve of festival; but for reliability to eat with him or buy from him — permitted in other matters even intentional transgression knowing it is forbidden; if regarding that matter he does not appear as transgression to people, plainly others should not rely since he thinks it permitted — as Rama concludes here; nevertheless what is the practical difference — he is not called suspected.
turei-zahav.8#_: Even under oath. For he is already suspected to transgress the oath being under oath from Sinai; and even though Sinai oath is for past, since under oath and also sinned he is worse; and no distinction future vs past oath except monetary matters, not prohibition.
turei-zahav.11#_: He does not make libation wine. The reason: a gentile's statement is plausible as false; when he says he believes it is for evil inclination's pleasure and our faith is good and true; and when he tells us he is a Jew he says wholeheartedly because our faith is faithful and true and the matter is plain that for all prohibitions he is not believed; only he does not make yayin nesech being truly a Jew; but for reliability in prohibitions since he worships idols for desire plainly not believed.
turei-zahav.13#א: What he ate he ate, etc. So in mishnah Bechorot end of chapter Kol Pesulei HaMukdashin; Rashi: returns money because of penalty of safek prohibition; appears only when known he knew they were forbidden and sold intentionally we penalize; if not, perhaps inadvertent; and though seif 17 butcher has no excuse — that is prohibition not money; Taz appears even safek tereifah — what he ate he ate and returns money, eating not considered benefit.
turei-zahav.13#ב: Rabbinic matters. If produce still exists — so it must be; this is Rambam's view that in d'rabbanan prohibition once he ate and benefited he does not return.
turei-zahav.14#א: Its law like selling rabbinic prohibitions. Reason: d'oraisa no lung check needed without defect before us — we rely on majority kosher animals; Sages required checking; what he ate seller deducts; nevertheless what not eaten he returns for mistaken transaction; though regarding butcher Choshen Mishpat exempt in doubt because you come for his act — only obligate certainly; here between buyer and seller even doubt is mistaken transaction; Achai incident needle in lung after cutting — compared to butcher case — not per my reason; nevertheless well judged perhaps eaten before known tereifah; or needle swallowed before purchase; if within seller's permission after slaughter clearly mistaken transaction; if ate selling butcher exempt — no penalty since he did not know; unlike mistaken transaction while meat remains must return for defect; if seller knew and sold — buyer returns even if ate, unlike Levush.
turei-zahav.14#ב: And if he sold from an animal, etc. Even though Shulchan Aruch said if tereifah from improper lung check and buyer ate seller deducts — only where d'oraisa no check needed without defect; if defect exists automatically requires check d'oraisa and cannot check — even if buyer ate seller returns for selling doubt d'oraisa prohibition; only if seller knew doubt then penalty; if not, return only if not eaten from mistaken transaction.
turei-zahav.15#_: To a place where he is not recognized, etc. Maharshal: nowadays generation is unrestrained and if sages see he cannot exile because dependents hang on him they give repentance locally with restriction; one transgression makes him a stumbling block — warn him; nevertheless forbid vessels retroactively in doubt even first time; Shach: even first sale of forbidden removes him; Mechaber seif 17; Choshen Mishpat some say butcher and teacher need presumption before removal — Ribash: there only monetary loss or misled/inadvertent; suspected feeding prohibition — remove immediately; Rashba: butcher tereifah no inadvertent excuse; vessels siman 1; Beit Yosef Choshen Mishpat siman 34 Rambam: inspector for self needs exile after repentance; for others no monetary benefit — repentance suffices.
turei-zahav.18#_: By accepting fellowship rules. Explained in Bechorot chapter Ad Kamah that he accepts ascetic practices the majority do not practice.
turei-zahav.19#_: And all this does not apply to suspected, etc. Written per Beit Yosef — perhaps they were lenient only in their prohibitions; after Meshoreret HaBayit was revealed we see Rashba siman 2 regarding habitual sinner for appetite who said expert slaughtered — believed in d'oraisa slaughter; likewise Meshoreret HaBayit explicitly even d'oraisa we rely when he says explicitly so-and-so expert, for he fears; proof from Demai; cheese learns from Demai; all learn Demai; suspected not worse than habitual sinner for appetite; Rashba only requires explicit expert for cheese and slaughter; second law gift — person does not give from own in another's name — even d'oraisa as siman 118 thigh; Beit Yosef thought Rashba only on gentile cheese d'rabbanan — nothing, Rashba teaches even d'rabbanan need explicit expert; second law not only fear — even strong-handed person; gift-giver mentions expert's name; Perishah wrongly split d'oraisa vs d'rabbanan — refuted by Meshoreret HaBayit; resolves difficulties siman 2 and Demai and thigh; Beit Yosef brought Rambam believed on others' tithes — challenged from Demai mishnah; answer collusion concern; after Shabbat must tithe; Rashba believed on others' testimony; difficult Rambam believed in all cases — Raavad, Kesef Mishneh, Yerushalmi guest leniency; Tosafot guest only when not recognized; Rambam only stranger; still difficult why believed here on others; rule like Rashbag except Bechor penalty; Demai stranger cases; suspected believed on others except collusion; not like Raah; practical: suspected not worse than Demai; Taz disputes Rama d'oraisa on cheese purchase — Meshoreret HaBayit refutes; siman 2 slaughter when says expert so-and-so; siman 86 eggs seller himself; siman 118 thigh d'oraisa reasoning; habitual sinner for appetite not before blind; suspected thinks permitted — not believed d'oraisa; Perishah wrong on self-eating slaughterer — siman 2 refutes.
turei-zahav.20#_: Suspected. Shach: habitual sinner for that matter not others — unlike Bach. Taz: Beit Yosef brought Rambam suspected and gentile believed on others' tithes — no sin without self-benefit; disputes — we establish suspected not judged or testifies; so rule in practice.
